## Lee — going halves on a dumper

I reckon it’s worth us buying this secondhand dumper rather than paying to hire one every time we’ve got a bigger job. We’ve worked together long enough — 15 years now — so I’ve put the figures down for you to have a proper look at.

### What we’re spending now

We’ve hired the tracked dumper from Sittingbourne for **14 days this year at £85 a day**. That’s **£1,190 just in hire**, plus £30 delivery each time. We’ve spent roughly **£1,600 all in**, and we’ve got nothing to show for it once it goes back.

The bloke in Faversham wants **£1,650 ono** for his **2019 500kg tracked dumper**. He says it had new tracks last spring. At the asking price, that’s **£825 each**, possibly less if there’s a deal to be done.

At this year’s use, the purchase price is about a year’s hire money. Even at half that use, it’s roughly two years. That’s **before servicing and repairs**, so it isn’t the whole cost, but it’s a decent starting point.

### Why I think we’d use it

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring. Having our own means we can get started when we’re ready, rather than waiting for availability or a delivery driver. That one turning up at 11 cost us half the morning.

And when they didn’t have one in September, we ended up barrowing six tonnes of muck at Hernhill. Two extra days on the job, and your back was gone for a week. I’d rather not repeat that.

### How we’d split it

- **Purchase and servicing: 50/50.**
- **Fuel and normal running costs:** paid for by whichever job it’s being used on.
- **Ordinary wear-and-tear repairs:** split equally.
- **If one of us breaks it through misuse, he pays.**

It can live under cover in my lean-to at the yard. If owning it doesn’t work out, we can sell it and split the money. They seem to hold their value, though obviously we might not get every penny back.

**Come and look at it with me this Saturday**, before someone else has it. We’ll check it over and see it working — no need to buy it if it’s not right.
